Headline: 6% Bonus Shares of Garima Bikas Bank Limited Listed in NEPSE
Full Content:
34,08,310.40 unit bonus shares of
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL)
have been listed in NEPSE.
The company convened it's 19th AGM on 27th Kartik, 2082, and endorsed a 10.53% dividend for FY 2081/82. The company decided to distribute a 6% bonus share and a 4.53% cash dividend (including tax). The same bonus shares are now listed in NEPSE.

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank and ACAN Sign MoU to Provide Special Loan Facilities for Chartered Accountants
Full Content:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has signed an agreement with the Association of Chartered Accountants of Nepal (ACAN) to offer various loan facilities to ACAN-affiliated chartered accountants at attractive interest rates. The agreement was signed by GBBL CEO Madhav Prasad Upadhaya and ACAN President Anup Nepal.
Under the agreement, ACAN members can access credit card facilities ranging from NPR 75,000 to NPR 500,000 with minimal documentation and obtain unsecured personal professional loans of up to NPR 1.5 million after completing the required procedures.
Additionally, the bank will provide home loans and vehicle loans at competitive interest rates to ACAN members. Currently, GBBL is offering housing loans starting from 6.49 percent and SME and business loans from 5.99 percent. With a nationwide network of 126 branches, 51 ATMs, and advanced digital banking services, Garima Bikas Bank serves around 950,000 customers across Nepal, delivering simple, secure, and quality banking services.

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank Unveils New Logo and Branding
Full Content:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has updated its official logo and seal effective Magh 1, 2082, as part of its long-term strategy to strengthen corporate identity. The logo change was approved at the 29th Annual General Meeting on Kartik 27, 2082, followed by completion of necessary legal formalities.
The new logo represents the bank’s modern, simple identity and its commitment to trustworthy and high-quality banking services. GBBL expressed gratitude to all customers and stakeholders and reaffirmed its commitment to providing more effective and quality banking services in the future.

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank Wins Digital Transaction Excellence Awards
Full Content:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited has been honored with the ‘Excellence in Digital Transactions FY 2081/82’ and ‘Excellence in Nepalpay QR Transaction FY 2081/82’ awards at the 17th anniversary program of Nepal Clearing House Limited.
The bank received the awards for achieving the highest digital and QR transactions among development banks in fiscal year 2081/82. CEO Madhav Prasad Upadhaya accepted the awards at the Kathmandu event.
Garima Bikas Bank currently serves nearly 9 lakh customers through 126 branches, 51 ATMs, and modern digital banking services nationwide.

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank Celebrates 19th Anniversary with Blood Donation and CSR Initiatives
Full Content:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) celebrated its 19th anniversary with extensive social responsibility programs. On 7 Mangsir 2082, the bank organized blood donation drives in 8 locations, collecting 602 units, and carried out 19 CSR initiatives, including distributing educational materials, school uniforms, water filters, and sanitation supplies across 16 schools and various institutions.
Additionally, the second edition of the Garima Road Race on 6 Mangsir saw participation of over 1,000 runners under the theme "Healthy Lifestyle through Sports." GBBL aims to continue such programs annually, expressing gratitude to its stakeholders for their support.

Headline: Garima Road Race 2082 Successfully Concludes on GBBL’s 19th Anniversary
Full Content:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) celebrated its 19th anniversary by successfully organizing the Garima Road Race 2082 on Mangsir 6, promoting the slogan “Sports for a Healthy Lifestyle.” Over 1,000 runners participated across six categories, open, corporate, and veteran races for both men and women. In the 10 km open race, Olympian Santoshi Shrestha and Nepal Army’s Rajan Rokaya secured first place for women and men respectively, with Nepal Army athletes dominating several positions.
Cash prizes, medals, and certificates were awarded to top finishers in all categories. The event saw participation from GBBL executives, shareholders, local representatives, and journalists. GBBL also announced that on Mangsir 7, it will hold blood donation drives in eight locations and CSR programs in 19 locations nationwide as part of the anniversary celebrations.

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank to Host Second “Garima Road Race 2082” Promoting Fitness and Inclusivity
Full Content:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited is organizing the second edition of the Garima Road Race 2082 on Mangsir 6, 2082 B.S., to celebrate its 19th anniversary. Held under the slogan “Sports for Health,” the event promotes fitness and community engagement. Following last year’s successful race with 650 participants, this year’s edition expects around 1,000 runners and introduces a new Veteran category for women aged 45+ and men aged 50+.
The race includes three categories, Open (10 KM), Corporate (5 KM), and Veteran (5 KM), with attractive cash prizes up to NPR 50,000. The event will start and conclude at Baluwatar, Kathmandu, with distinct routes for each category. Registration can be completed easily via the Khalti App between Kartik 28 and Mangsir 4, with a nominal fee of NPR 20.

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank Unveils Book Closure Date for its 10.53% Dividend; Calls AGM on Kartik 27
Full Content:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL)
has called its 19th AGM on 27th Kartik, 2082. The meeting will be held in Hotel Pokhara Grande, Pokhara, Kaski, starting at 11:00 am that day.
According to the proposal, the bank plans to distribute a total dividend of 10.53%, which includes a 6% bonus share and 4.53% cash dividend (including tax on bonus shares) from the accumulated profits. The proposed dividend will be distributed to shareholders after approval from Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) and endorsement from the bank’s upcoming 19th Annual General Meeting (AGM). Headline: Garima Bikas Bank Proposes 10.53% Dividend for FY 2081/82
Full Content:

According to the proposal, the bank plans to distribute a total dividend of 10.53%, which includes a 6% bonus share and 4.53% cash dividend (including tax on bonus shares) from the accumulated profits. Headline: Garima Bikas Bank Launches Virtual Credit Card on Mobile Banking App for Safe and Convenient Payments
Full Content:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL), in collaboration with the Fonepay network, has launched a Virtual Credit Card service through its mobile banking app, Garima Digi Batuwa. Full Content:

Headline: Comprehensive Analysis of Fourth Quarter Reports for FY 2081/82: A Closer Look at Development Banks in Nepal
Full Content:
The fourth-quarter reports for the fiscal year 2081/82 have been publicly disclosed by 15 out of 16 development banks. These reports provide a comprehensive overview of their financial health. Karnali Development Bank Limited has not published its report as Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has declared it a "problematic institution" and placed its management under direct NRB control. Share trading of Karnali Development Bank has also been suspended.
This analysis aims to meticulously evaluate the financial performance of Nepal's development banks, categorized as "B" class financial institutions, using the unaudited third-quarter reports for the 2081/82 fiscal year.
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) currently lists 16 development banks, divided into National-level and Regional-level entities. Our focus is on assessing the performance of these "B" class financial institutions, drawing insights from the recently released quarter-end reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period, amounting to Rs. 153.74 Crores. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit, which amounts to Rs. 131.04 Crores.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs.68.86 Crores. In terms of growth in net profit, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) achieved the highest growth margin of 201.97% for Q4 of FY 81/82.
At the regional level, Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported the highest growth in net profit at 287.60% for Q4 of FY 81/82.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.04 Arba among all the development banks, with Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) holding the second-highest paid-up capital at Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) reported the highest reserve and surplus, totaling Rs. 4.92 Arba. Following MNBBL is Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) with a reserve of Rs. 3.03 Arba. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) holds the third position with a reserve of 2.9 Arba.
Meanwhile, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC), Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU), and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
Among B-class institutions, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with a total deposit of Rs. 1.17 Kharba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a deposit of Rs. 90.12 Arba. The overall development banks have collected a total deposit of Rs. 4.1 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
As of Q4 2081/82, total loans and advances of development banks reached Rs. 4.82 Kharba, with an average loan of Rs. 32.18 Arba. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) disbursed the highest loan amount, totaling Rs. 97.52 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 69.32 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Limited (SHINE) disbursed Rs. 546.93 Arba, ranking third.
Net interest income:
In terms of Net Interest Income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with Rs. 4.55 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 3.64 Arba, and Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank  with Rs. 2.24 Arba. Out of the 15 banks, 8 reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside funds as loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments for several borrowers.
Total impairment charges amount to Rs. 4.47 Arba for loans and other losses. Among National Level banks, Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) shows the highest impairment charge at Rs. 128.34 Crores, with Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) also holding high provisions at Rs. 67.97 Crores.
At the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported a reversal in impairment charges.
Annualized Earnings per share:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) topped the annualized EPS list at Rs. 23.07 per share, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) followed by  with Rs. 21.82 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) at Rs.192.73 per share, followed by Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) with Rs. 169.95 per share and Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) at Rs.168.13 per share. The average net worth per share of the 15 banks is Rs.137.55.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio indicates how much investors are paying for each rupee of the firm’s earnings. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio at 18.57 times, whereas Jyoti bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) reports the highest P/E ratio at 1248.34 times.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loans indicate credit risk for banks. Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has the lowest NPL ratio at 0.28%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the highest at 50.97%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) reported the highest CAR at 31.54% while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reported the negative CAR at 7.84%.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 6.61%, while Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest at 3.87%.
CD Ratio:
The Credit-Deposit Ratio shows how much deposit money has been used as loans. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) reports the highest CD ratio of 89.62%, and Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) has the lowest at 63.04%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
The base rate, the minimum interest rate banks charge, is highest at Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) with 16.24% and lowest at Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) with 6.02%. Meanwhile, Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) reports the highest interest spread rate of 4.60%, and Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has the lowest at 3.96%.

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank Reports 201.97% Surge in Net Profit in Q4 FY 2081/82; Impairment Charges Fallen By 68.56%
Full Content:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL)
has reported a significant growth in its financial performance for the fourth quarter of FY 2081/82.
The development bank posted a net profit of Rs. 1.31 Arba, marking a 201.97% increase from Rs. 43.39 crore in the same period last year. The rise was supported by an improvement in net interest income, which climbed 9.91% to Rs. 3.64 Arba compared to Rs. 3.31 Arba in Q4 2080/81.
Deposits grew by 6.96% to Rs. 90.12 Arba, while loans and advances increased by 7.32% to Rs. 69.32 Arba. The bank’s operating profit surged by 195.58% to Rs. 1.89 Arba. Impairment charges for loans and advances fell sharply by 68.56% to Rs. 53.79 crore.
Key financial ratios improved during the review period. The capital adequacy ratio stood at 13.47%, while NPL declined to 4.72% from 4.85% a year earlier. The cost of funds decreased to 4.84% from 6.64%. Annualized EPS increased to Rs. 23.07, and net worth per share reached Rs. 164.17.

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank Promotes Green Heritage with Bar-Peepal Plantation on Harishayani Ekadashi
Full Content:
On the occasion of Harishayani Ekadashi (Ashadh 22, 2082), Garima Bikas Bank Limited organized a tree plantation program as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), planting Bodhi (Peepal) and Banyan trees at six religious and environmentally significant locations across Kaski, Syangja, and Dang districts.
The initiative saw active participation from local representatives, social workers, employees, shareholders, and the public. The bank believes such actions aid in environmental conservation, promote green development, and preserve religious heritage, with plans to develop these areas into traditional "Bar-Peepal Chautaris." The bank aims to continue such initiatives to support sustainable development and environmental balance.

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank Joins NEPALPAY Card Network and National Card Switch
Full Content:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited has officially entered into an agreement with Nepal Clearing House Limited (NCHL) to join the NPS-National Card Switch (NCS) and the domestic NEPALPAY Card scheme. The agreement was signed on July 3, 2025, by Mr. Madhav Prasad Upadhaya, CEO of Garima Bikas Bank, and Mr. Neelesh Man Singh Pradhan, CEO of NCHL.
This collaboration follows NCHL's recent announcement of the readiness of the NPS-NCS infrastructure, which is designed to enable local card issuance and transaction processing through the NEPALPAY Card. Once commercially rolled out, Garima Bikas Bank will be able to issue and acquire NEPALPAY Cards for its customers, reducing reliance on international schemes and promoting cost-effective, interoperable domestic transactions.
As a leading development bank, Garima Bikas Bank serves customers through 125 branches, 1 extension counter, and 51 ATMs. The bank's onboarding into NEPALPAY is expected to strengthen Nepal’s digital payment landscape and foster innovation in the local card ecosystem.

Headline: ICRA Nepal Reaffirms BBB- Rating for Garima Bikas Bank with Negative Watch Status
Full Content:
ICRA Nepal has reaffirmed Garima Bikas Bank Limited's issuer rating at [ICRANP-IR] BBB- (Triple B minus), maintaining the status of "Watch with Negative Implications."
This rating suggests a moderate level of safety in meeting financial obligations, indicating moderate credit risk.
The rating reflects the bank's general creditworthiness and is not specific to any particular financial instrument. The BBB- rating denotes the lower end of the moderate credit quality spectrum.

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank Expands Services with Two New Branches in Syangja
Full Content:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited, known for delivering reliable and quality banking services from rural to urban areas, has inaugurated two new branches in Biruwa and Arjun Chaupari of Syangja district on 31st Baishakh 2082.
The Biruwa branch was jointly inaugurated by Biruwa Rural Municipality Chairperson Suryabahadur Kunwar and Bank Chairman Dilip Pratap Khand, while the Arjun Chaupari branch was jointly opened by Vice-Chairperson Sapana Gurung and Chairman Khand.
The inauguration events saw active participation from local representatives, traders, and the general public.
The bank is committed to providing excellent services to residents, businesses, and institutions through these new branches and aims to play a significant role in the area's economic growth. With 125 branches, 1 extension counter, and 50 ATMs across Nepal, Garima Bikas Bank now serves around 900,000 customers nationwide.

Headline: Comparative Analysis of Development Banks in Q2 FY 2081/82: Profits, Capital, and Ratios Unveiled

Karnali Development Bank Limited has not published its report as Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has declared it a "problematic institution" and placed its management under direct NRB control. Share trading of Karnali Development Bank has also been suspended.
This analysis aims to meticulously evaluate the financial performance of Nepal's development banks, categorized as "B" class financial institutions, using the unaudited second-quarter reports for the 2081/82 fiscal year.
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) currently lists 16 development banks, divided into National-level and Regional-level entities. Our focus is on assessing the performance of these "B" class financial institutions, drawing insights from the recently released quarter-end reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Garima Bikas Bank (GBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period, amounting to Rs. 54.93 Crores. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit, which amounts to Rs. 50.31 Crores.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs. 33.09 Crores. In terms of growth in net profit, Jyoti Bikas Bank (JBBL) achieved the highest growth margin of 147.58% for Q2 of FY 81/82.
At the regional level, Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported the highest growth in net profit at 93.56% for Q2 of FY 81/82.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.05 Arba among all the development banks, with Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) holding the second-highest paid-up capital at Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) reported the highest reserve and surplus, totaling Rs. 3.89 Arba. Following MNBBL is Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) with a reserve of Rs. 3.05 Arba. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) holds the third position with a reserve of 2.94 Arba.

Deposits from Customers:

Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) disbursed the highest loan amount, totaling Rs. 95.64 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 67.66 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Limited (SHINE) disbursed Rs. 54.84 Arba, ranking third.
Net interest income:
In terms of Net Interest Income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with Rs. 2.91 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 1.84 Arba, and Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE) with Rs. 1.29 Arba. Out of the 15 banks, 8 reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside funds as loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments for several borrowers.

At the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC), Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL), and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported a reversal in impairment charges.
Annualized Earnings per share:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) topped the annualized EPS list at Rs. 19.34 per share, followed by Kamana Sewa Bank Limited (KSBBL) with Rs. 18.37 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) at Rs. 181.39 per share, followed by Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) with Rs. 165.35 per share and Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) at Rs. 157.84 per share. The average net worth per share of the 15 banks is Rs. 132.15.

The P/E ratio indicates how much investors are paying for each rupee of the firm’s earnings. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio at 20.12 times, whereas Corporate Development Bank Limited reports the highest P/E ratio at 407.7 times.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loans indicate credit risk for banks. Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has the lowest NPL ratio at 1.74%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the highest at 43.69%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) reported the highest CAR at 35.21%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reported the lowest at 1.19%.
Others:

Headline: Financial Showdown: A Comparative Deep Dive into Development Banks' Q4 Performance for FY 2080/81
Full Content:
The fourth-quarter reports for the fiscal year 2080/81 have been publicly disclosed by 16 development banks, with the notable exception of
Karnali Development Bank (KRBL)
, which has yet to release its quarter-end report. These reports provide a comprehensive overview of their financial health. This analysis aims to meticulously evaluate the financial performance of Nepal's development banks, categorized as "B" class financial institutions, using the unaudited fourth-quarter reports for the 2080/81 fiscal year.
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) currently lists 16 development banks, divided into National-level and Regional-level entities. Our focus is on assessing the performance of these "B" class financial institutions, drawing insights from the recently released quarter-end reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period amounting to Rs. 1.27 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit which amounts to Rs. 1.13 Arba.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs. 69.74 Crores. In terms of growth in Net profit, Shangrila Development Bank (SADBL) has obtained the highest growth margin of 92.47% for the Q4 of FY 80/81.
Coming towards the regional level, Corporate Development Bank (CORBL) has reported the highest growth in net profit of 194.23% for Q4 of FY 80/81.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.05 Arba among all the development banks. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
The reserve is the amount that is retained by the company from its profits to promote future growth.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest reserve and surplus which amounts to Rs. 3.50 Arba. MNBBL is followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a total reserve of Rs. 3.26 Arba. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) has secured the third position with a reserve of 3.11 Arba.
Whereas, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC), Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
In B-class institution, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has topped the list with a total deposit of Rs. 1.09 Kharba. This list is followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a total deposit of Rs. 84.25 Arba.
The overall development bank has collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.94 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Till Q4 2080/2081, total loans and advances of development banks stood at Rs. 4.61 Kharba. The average loan stood at Rs. 30.78 Arba.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has disbursed the highest amount of loans which amounts to Rs. 91.90 Arba. Following the list, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has disbursed a total loan of Rs. 66.01 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Limited (SHINE) has disbursed a loan of Rs. 52.17 Arba which puts it in third place.
Net interest income:
Net Interest Income is the core business revenue which is calculated by subtracting the cost related to the deposits from the income from loans and advances.
In terms of Net interest income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) tops the list with a total of Rs. 4.18 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest net interest income amounting to Rs. 3.46 Arba. GBBL is followed by Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) which has reported a net interest income of Rs. 2.36 Arba.
Out of the 16 banks, 8 banks have reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside a certain amount in loan loss provision and have delayed the loan repayment of several borrowers. A total of Rs 3.83 Arba has been shown in an impairment charge for a loan and other losses.
In the National Level, Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has the highest impairment charge for a loan and other losses with Rs. 95.17 Crores. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) also has higher provisions amounting to Rs. 70.92 Crores.
In the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) have reported the lowest impairment charges for this period.
Earnings per share:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) topped the list in terms of EPS amounting to Rs. 20 per share. Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has the second-highest EPS with Rs. 18.38 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) with Rs. 188.48 per share. This is followed by Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) with a net worth per share of Rs. 164.48 per share. Similarly, Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) reported a net worth of Rs. 160.44 per share.
The average net worth per share comes at Rs. 133.10 per share when we factor in the net worth per share of 16 banks.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio tells investors what they are paying for each rupee of earnings of the firm. The lower the ratio, the better the deal.
In terms of the P/E ratio, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio of 19.25 times. Meanwhile, Narayani Development Bank Limited reported the highest P/E of 685.79 times.
One should always check the fundamentals of the company and if they find the bad fundamentals then there is a reason for the lower valuation. Also, the PE is calculated as per the quarter-end closing price of the respective companies. In today's date, the price differs in the secondary market.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loan indicates the risk of credit provided by the bank to its clients. A higher NPL indicates that the bank might be at risk.
In terms of NPL, Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has the lowest ratio with an NPL of 0.97%, and on the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has reported the highest NPL of 35%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
In terms of the Capital Adequacy ratio (CAR), Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) seems to have reported the highest CAR of 38.65%, while Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) has the lowest CAR of 6.58%.
CAR is the ratio of a bank's capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets and current liabilities.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
The term cost of funds refers to how much banks and financial institutions spend in order to acquire money to lend to their customers. The lower the cost of funds, the better because it ultimately reduces the cost of banks. As per reports, Corporate Development Bank Limited (LBBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 7.71%, whereas Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest cost of funds at 5.55%.
CD Ratio:
The CD ratio refers to the credit-deposit ratio in banking parlance. It tells how much of the money banks have raised in the form of deposits has been deployed as loans. Similarly, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest CD ratio of 85.83%, whereas Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has reported the lowest CD ratio of 60.56%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
Base rate is defined as the minimum interest rate set by the NRB below which banks are not permitted to lend to their customers. Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reports the highest base rate of 15.33%, and Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest base rate of 8%.
Likewise, the net interest rate spread represents the variance between the interest rate disbursed to depositors and the interest accrued from loans extended to consumers by a bank. Among the majority of development banks, a consistent interest spread rate of 4.58% has been upheld, with the highest reported at 4.59%.

Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) celebrated the 12th series of Global Money Week by organizing various programs aimed at enhancing financial literacy among children and youth.
With the slogan "Protect Your Money, Secure our Future," the bank collaborated with schools, colleges, and educational associations across seven provinces of Nepal.

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank Appoints New CEO: Mr. Madhav Prasad Upadhaya
Full Content:

Mr. Madhav Prasad Upadhaya
as the Chief Executive Officer for a tenure of 4 years, effective from 1st Baisakh 2081.

Headline: Nepal Rastra Bank Imposes Disciplinary Measures Against Six Financial Institutions for Regulatory Violations
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has taken stern disciplinary measures against six financial institutions, including Global IME Bank, Prabhu Bank, Himalayan Bank, Muktinath Bikas Bank, Garima Bikas Bank, and Reliance Finance, for violating mandatory regulations.
Global IME Bank (GBIME) is directed to refund excess funds charged as premiums, surpassing the allowed limits. The bank breached regulations by increasing the Risk Premium rate in the fiscal year 2079/80, contrary to the directive. The directive emphasizes the importance of setting aside funds for potential loan losses, addressing issues like misusing loans, inactive businesses, Debt-to-Equity Ratio non-compliance, and inadequate debt recovery.
Prabhu Bank (PRVU) faces penalties for improper loan classification and insufficient risk mitigation systems. Violations include incorrect loan loss categorization, failure to allocate funds for loan recovery, and an increase in the Risk Premium rate against guidelines. Additionally, inaccuracies in reporting loan risks under the Capital Adequacy Framework 2015 were noted.
Himalayan Bank (HBL) is under scrutiny for miscalculating its capital adequacy ratio, resulting in reduced primary capital and reporting higher risk-weighted assets. Despite holding necessary permits, the bank failed to categorize loans and allocate provisions as per Unified Directive 2079, Directive No. 2/079.
Muktinath Bikas Bank (MNBBL) incurs a Rs. 10 lakhs fine for non-compliance with ongoing due diligence. Directors of Garima Bikas Bank (GBBL) and Reliance Finance (RLFL) receive official warnings for regulatory breaches.
Garima Bikas Bank's Director, Dr. Ananda Prasad Shrestha, and others collected funds through a joint account intending to open an insurance company. Despite applications and funds from various institutions, insufficient oversight was noted. Dr. Ananda Prasad Shrestha is cautioned by NRB, and the CEO of the institution is also warned.
Reliance Finance's Chairman, Kush Prasad Mally, and others used joint and personal accounts for individual business transactions. Due to irregular Customer Due Diligence (CDD) updates and perceived weaknesses in institutional and managerial conduct, Chairman Kush Prasad Mally is cautioned by NRB.

Headline: Comparative Analysis of Development Banks in Q2 FY 2080/81: Profits, Capital, and Ratios Unveiled
Full Content:
The second-quarter reports for the ongoing fiscal year 2080/81 have been disclosed by 15 development banks, providing a comprehensive overview of their financial status. Among them, Karnali Development Bank (KRBL) stands as the sole exception, as it has yet to release its report. This analysis will particularly delve into assessing the financial performance of Development Banks of Nepal, a "B" class financial institution, based on the unaudited 2nd quarterly report of the 2080/81 fiscal year.
NEPSE currently lists a total of 16 development banks, each falling into distinct categories - National-level banks and Regional-level banks. Our focus lies specifically on scrutinizing the performance of B-class financial institutions within this framework, drawing insights from the disclosed second-quarter reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period amounting to Rs. 51.26 Crores. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit which amounts to Rs. 42 Crores.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs. 37.12 Crores. In terms of growth in Net profit, Jyoti Bikas Bank (JBBL) has obtained a growth margin of 190.73% for the Q2 of FY 80/81.
Coming towards the regional level, Green Development Bank (GRDBL) has reported the highest growth in net profit of 346.81% while Excel Development Bank (EDBL) reported the highest decline in net profit of 400.69% in the Q2 of FY 80/81.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.05 Arba among all the development banks. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 5.67 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
The reserve is the amount that is retained by the company from its profits to promote future growth.
Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) has reported the highest reserve and surplus which amounts to Rs. 2.73 Arba. LBBL is followed by Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) with a total reserve of Rs. 2.61 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has secured the third position with a reserve of 2.58 Arba.
Whereas, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
In B-class institution, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has topped the list with a total deposit of Rs. 1.12 Kharba. This list is followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a total deposit of Rs. 78.58 Arba.
The overall development bank has collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.65 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Till Q2 2080/2081, total loans and advances of development banks stood at Rs. 4.59 Kharba. The average loan stood at Rs. 30.59 Arba.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has disbursed the highest amount of loans which amounts to Rs. 96.30 Arba. Following the list, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has disbursed a total loan of Rs. 63.91 Arba. Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has disbursed a loan of Rs. 50.81 Arba which puts it in third place.
Net interest income:
Net Interest Income is the core business revenue which is calculated by subtracting the cost related to the deposits from the income from loans and advances.
In terms of Net interest income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) tops the list with a total of Rs. 2.08 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest net interest income amounting to Rs. 1.80 Arba. GBBL is followed by Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) which has reported a net interest income of Rs. 1.12 Arba.
Out of the 15 banks, 8 banks have reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside a certain amount in loan loss provision and have delayed the loan repayment of several borrowers. A total of Rs 3.19 Arba has been shown in an impairment charge for a loan and other losses.
In the National Level, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest impairment charge for a loan and other losses with Rs. 78.63 Crores. Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) also has higher provisions amounting to Rs. 54.75 Crores.
In the regional level, Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) have reported the lowest impairment charges for this period.
Earnings per share:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) topped the list in terms of EPS amounting to Rs. 18.06 per share. Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has the second-highest EPS with Rs. 15.78 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) with Rs. 177.84 per share. This is followed by Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) with a net worth per share of Rs. 154.04 per share. Similarly, Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) reported a net worth of Rs. 152.08 per share.
The average net worth per share comes at Rs. 127.45 per share when we factor in the net worth per share of 15 banks.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio tells investors what they are paying for each rupee of earnings of the firm. The lower the ratio, the better the deal.
In terms of the P/E ratio, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio of 21.37 times. Meanwhile, Corporate Development Bank Limited reported the highest P/E of 110.11 times from the regional level.
One should always check the fundamentals of the company and if they find the bad fundamentals then there is a reason for the lower valuation. Also, the PE is calculated as per the quarter-end closing price of the respective companies. In today's date, the price differs in the secondary market.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loan indicates the risk of credit provided by the bank to its clients. A higher NPL indicates that the bank might be at risk.
In terms of NPL, Sindhu Bikas Bank Limited (SINDU) has the lowest ratio with an NPL of 1.05%, and on the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has reported the highest NPL of 27.75%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
In terms of the Capital Adequacy ratio (CAR), Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) seems to have reported the highest CAR of 44.77%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest CAR of 9.46%.
CAR is the ratio of a bank's capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets and current liabilities.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
The term cost of funds refers to how much banks and financial institutions spend in order to acquire money to lend to their customers. The lower the cost of funds, the better because it ultimately reduces the cost of banks. As per reports, Green Development Bank Limited (GRDBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 9.32%, whereas Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest cost of funds at 7.44%.
CD Ratio:
The CD ratio refers to the credit-deposit ratio in banking parlance. It tells how much of the money banks have raised in the form of deposits has been deployed as loans. Similarly, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has reported the highest CD ratio of 91.20%, whereas Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has reported the lowest CD ratio of 65.86%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
Base rate is defined as the minimum interest rate set by the NRB below which banks are not permitted to lend to their customers. Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reports the highest base rate of 17.64%, and Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest base rate of 10.22%.
Likewise, the net interest rate spread represents the variance between the interest rate disbursed to depositors and the interest accrued from loans extended to consumers by a bank. Among the majority of development banks, a consistent interest spread rate of 4.59% has been upheld, with the highest reported at 4.60%.

Headline: Central Bank Takes Swift Action: Penalties Imposed on Development Banks and Finance Company
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has taken regulatory actions against five development banks and finance companies within the first quarter of the ongoing fiscal year.
As of the end of Ashwin, the Central Bank has imposed penalties on four development banks—Garima Bikas Bank (GBBL), Excel Development (EDBL), Karnali Development (KRBL), and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU)—and one finance company, Reliance Finance (RLFL). The penalties were in response to various violations of rules and laws outlined by the Central Bank.
The Central Bank disclosed that Excel Development Bank had neglected to conduct a thorough analysis of loan details, including the purpose, area of utilization, interest repayment basis, and loan amount distribution to unrelated entities. Consequently, the bank faced fines for misusing the loan amount and failing to exercise due diligence in the loan approval process.
Garima Bikas Bank, on the other hand, is under a one-year prohibition from holding or transacting securities following its involvement in providing share mortgage loans within a year after the former chairman of Kalika Microfinance Financial Institution resigned. This action aligns with the provisions of the Banking and Financial Institutions Act, 2073.
Karnali Development Bank received two reprimands from the Rastra Bank. The former CEO, Dinesh Kumar Rawat, was fined for serious violations of the Central Bank's instructions, acting against the interests of the institution, investors, depositors, and the public. The then chairman, Rajendrabir Rai, faced penalties for similar violations and indirect loan grants, both against the directives of the Nepal Rastra Bank.
Sindhu Bikas Bank faced dual actions due to its weak internal audit and operational risk management practices. The board of directors and various committees were alerted, as the institution's internal control system was found to be unsatisfactory and overall very weak.
Reliance Finance Company, targeted twice by the Rastra Bank, was penalized for disbursing loans over the debtor's business capacity, unsatisfactory loan projects, and misuse of funds. The board of directors and the director committee of Reliance Finance were notified under section 100 of the Nepal Rastra Bank Act, 2058.
Moreover, Reliance Finance's Chief Executive Officer, Samaj Prakash Shrestha, received a notification for recommending loan approval without proper inspection of mortgages, leading to misuse of funds against the interest of depositors and the intended project. The actions taken by the Nepal Rastra Bank aimed to address these regulatory violations and ensure the integrity of the financial institutions involved.

Headline: Government Records Rs. 12.5 Arba Profit Tax Collection from Mergers, Acquisitions, and FPOs as BFIs Meet Deadline
Full Content:
The Large Taxpayer Office revealed the collection of Rs. 12.5 Arba in profit tax from mergers, gains from acquisitions (bargain purchases), and profits derived from Follow-On Public Offerings (FPOs). This substantial amount was collected over the course of Friday and Saturday, with meticulous filings by numerous organizations.
On Friday, a total of 30 organizations contributed to this figure by filing taxes amounting to Rs. 11.3 Arba. The momentum continued on Saturday, with an additional 11 institutions filing taxes, totaling Rs. 1.44 Arba. Mr. Janak Sharma, the head of the Large Taxpayer Office, provided these details, emphasizing the proactive engagement of both public and private entities in fulfilling their tax obligations.
Crucially, it was revealed that among the 41 organizations that paid taxes on profits from FPO, 14 of them also paid taxes on profits from both FPO and bargain purchases resulting from mergers and acquisitions. The taxes collected fall under the purview of the current financial year, marking a significant boost in revenue generation.
The background of this revenue collection effort includes persistent recommendations from the Office of the Auditor General. Since the 57th annual report published in 2077 BS, concerns were raised regarding tax evasion related to premiums of FPO, gains from bargain purchases in mergers and acquisitions, and auction share sales. Despite the repeated concerns, the Ministry of Finance and the Inland Revenue Department initially overlooked the issue.
However, the 60th report of the Office reiterated the importance of recovering revenues from these sources. Finance Minister Dr. Prakash Sharan Mahat responded to these concerns by introducing an arrangement. According to this arrangement, companies paying taxes in premiums of FPO, bargain purchase gains of mergers and acquisitions, and auction share sales by the end of Mangsir would be exempted from fines and interests. The government intended to encourage timely payment of revenues.
This move faced legal scrutiny when 16 Banking and Financial Institutions (BFIs) filed a petition challenging the taxation initiative. The BFIs alleged that the government's decision to grant exemptions on fees and fines was unconstitutional, asserting that it amounted to imposing taxes against the constitutional framework. However, the constitutional bench of the Supreme Court recently dismissed the petition, upholding the government's position. The court ruled that the taxation did not constitute a levy on capital.
The formal announcement of the dismissal was made on last Thursday under the constitutional bench of Chief Justice Bishowambhar Prasad Shrestha, affirming the government's approach to taxation in this context.
BFIs were given a deadline to deposit the specified amount by the end of Mangsir, with the incentive that they would not be charged interest and penalties. As a result, companies proactively met this deadline, contributing significantly to the substantial revenue collection observed over the weekend.

Headline: Comprehensive Analysis of First Quarter Reports for FY 2080/81: A Closer Look at Development Banks in Nepal
Full Content:
The disclosure of first-quarter reports for the ongoing fiscal year 2080/81 from all 16 development banks offers a detailed understanding of their financial standing. This in-depth analysis will specifically focus on evaluating the financial performance of the "B" class financial institution, Development Banks of Nepal.
Currently listed on NEPSE, there are a total of 16 development banks. However, not all of the banks fall under the same category. The development banks can be categorized into two subcategories, National-level banks, and Regional-level banks. Therefore, our examination will center on dissecting the performance of B-class financial institutions based on the unaudited 1st quarterly report of the 2080/81 fiscal year.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period amounting to Rs. 22.88 Crores. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit which amounts to Rs. 20.15 Crores.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs. 19.17 Crores. In terms of growth in Net profit, Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank (KSBBL) has obtained a growth margin of 188% for the Q1 of FY 80/81.
Coming towards the regional level, Karnali Development Bank (KRBL) has reported the highest growth in net profit of 149.15% while Excel Development Bank (EDBL) reported the highest decline in net profit of 737% in the Q1 of FY 80/81. As per reports, 12 companies have reported a decline in net profit for this period.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 6.42 Arba among all the development banks. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 5.19 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
The reserve is the amount that is retained by the company from its profits to promote future growth.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest reserve and surplus which amounts to Rs. 3.2 Arba. MNBBL is followed by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) with a total reserve of Rs. 2.74 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has secured the third position with a reserve of 2.73 Arba.
Whereas, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
In B-class institution, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has topped the list with a total deposit of Rs. 1.16 Kharba. This list is followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a total deposit of Rs. 78.36 Arba. Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has secured the third position with a total deposit of Rs. 61.81 Arba.
The overall development bank has collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.63 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Till Q1 2080/2081, total loans and advances of development banks stood at Rs. 4.54 Kharba. The average loan stood at Rs. 28.37 Arba.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has disbursed the highest amount of loans which amounts to Rs. 96.74 Arba. Following the list, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has disbursed a total loan of Rs. 63.02 Arba. Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has disbursed a loan of Rs. 51.13 Arba which puts it in third place.
Net interest income:
Net Interest Income is the core business revenue which is calculated by subtracting the cost related to the deposits from the income from loans and advances.
In terms of Net interest income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) tops the list with a total of Rs. 1.04 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest net interest income amounting to Rs. 88.83 Crores. GBBL is followed by Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) which has reported a net interest income of Rs. 57.40 Crores.
Out of the 16 banks, 8 banks have reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside a certain amount in loan loss provision and have delayed the loan repayment of several borrowers. A total of Rs 1.91 Arba has been shown in an impairment charge for a loan and other losses.
In National Level, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest impairment charge for a loan and other losses with Rs. 36.15 Crores. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) also has higher provisions amounting to Rs. 35.35 Crores.
In the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has reported the lowest impairment charges for this period.
Earnings per share:
Karnali Development Bank Limited (KRBL) topped the list in terms of EPS amounting to Rs. 32.50 per share. LBBL Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) has the second-highest EPS with Rs. 20.49 per share.
Out of 16 development banks, 12 banks have reported above-industry average EPS.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) with Rs. 181.07 per share. This is followed by Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) with a net worth per share of Rs. 157.38 per share. Similarly, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) reported a net worth of Rs. 152.71 per share.
The average net worth per share comes at Rs. 128.33 per share when we factor in the net worth per share of all the 16 banks.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio tells investors what they are paying for each rupee of earnings of the firm. The lower the ratio, the better the deal.
In terms of the P/E ratio, Karnali Development Bank Limited (KRBL) has the lowest P/E ratio of 7.95 times. Meanwhile, Corporate Development Bank Limited reported the highest P/E of 105.53 times from the regional level.
One should always check the fundamentals of the company and if they find the bad fundamentals then there is a reason for the lower valuation. Also, the PE is calculated as per the quarter-end closing price of the respective companies. In today's date, the price differs in the secondary market.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loan indicates the risk of credit provided by the bank to its clients. A higher NPL indicates that the bank might be at risk.
In terms of NPL, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the lowest ratio with an NPL of 1.49%, and on the other hand, Saptakoshi Development Bank Limited (SAPDBL) has reported the highest NPL of 18.50%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
In terms of the Capital Adequacy ratio (CAR), Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) seems to have reported the highest CAR of 44.92%, while Karnali Development Bank Limited (KRBL) has the lowest CAR of 10.10%.
CAR is the ratio of a bank's capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets and current liabilities.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
The term cost of funds refers to how much banks and financial institutions spend in order to acquire money to lend to their customers. The lower the cost of funds, the better because it ultimately reduces the cost of banks. As per reports, Green Development Bank Limited (GRDBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 9.99%, whereas Sindhu Bikas Bank Limited (SINDU) has the lowest cost of funds at 8.36%.
CD Ratio:
The CD ratio refers to the credit-deposit ratio in banking parlance. It tells how much of the money banks have raised in the form of deposits has been deployed as loans. Similarly, Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) has reported the highest CD ratio of 93.07%, whereas Karnali Development Bank Limited (KRBL) has reported the lowest CD ratio of 75.78%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
Base rate is defined as the minimum interest rate set by the NRB below which banks are not permitted to lend to their customers. Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reports the highest base rate of 17.78%, and Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest base rate of 12%.
Similarly, the net interest rate spread is the difference between the interest rate a bank pays to depositors and the interest rate it receives from loans to consumers. Here,Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the highest interest spread of 5.12%.

Headline: NRB Reports Net Profits of Commercial and Development Banks Till Bhadra of FY 2080/81; GBIME Leading The Chart
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank has unveiled recent statistics covering the net profit of commercial banks, and development banks for up to the first two months of the current fiscal year 2080/81 i.e. Bhadra.
Commercial Banks
During the first two months of the fiscal year 2080/81, commercial banks in Nepal collectively earned a total net profit of Rs. 16.64 Arba.
Among these, Global IME Bank earned the highest net profit, surpassing all others, with Rs. 1.75 Arba. Similarly, Nabil Bank earned Rs.1.56 Arba, NIMB earned Rs. 1.48 Arba, Himalayan Bank earned Rs. 1.23 Arba, and Kumari Bank earned Rs. 1.14 Arba in net profits during this period. These five banks stood out with profits exceeding Rs. 1 Arba.
On the other hand, Nepal SBI Bank and Machhapuchchhre Bank reported the lowest net profits during this period, with Rs. 27.29 Crores and Rs. 37.63 Crores, respectively. Citizens Bank earned Rs. 44.31 Crores and Standard Chartered Bank reported a net profit of Rs. 48.45 Crores.
The net profit of other banks remained above Rs. 50 Crores.
Development Banks
The development banking sector in Nepal achieved a noteworthy net profit of Rs. 1.35 Arba, despite facing losses reported by four out of the 17 banks in this category. Muktinath Bikas Bank emerged as a standout performer, recording an impressive net profit of Rs. 31.28 crore, closely followed by Garima Bikas Bank, which earned Rs. 16.55 crore.
Conversely, Green Development Bank and Salapa reported the lowest profits in the sector, with earnings of Rs. 1.03 Crores and Rs. 40.10 Lakhs, respectively. Additionally, Narayani, Saptakoshi, Excel, and Miteri Development Bank faced challenges as they grappled with net losses during the period.

Headline: Banks and Financial Institutions Reduce Interest Rates for Baishakh
Full Content:
Banks and Financial Institutions have unveiled the interest rates profile for the month of Baishakh.
Commercial Banks:
The Chief Executive Officers of commercial banks' umbrella group, NBA, lowered the interest rates which shall be effective from Baishkah, 2080.
It has been decided to reduce the interest rate on personal deposits by 10%. The interest rate on fixed deposits has now decreased to single digits as a result of this move.
For commercial banks, the interest rate of one-year term deposits has decreased from 11 percent to 9.9 percent.
Along with this, the interest rate of institutional fixed deposits has remained at 7.99 percent. Similarly, the interest rate on savings has remained at 5.4 to 7.4 percent.
The rate of remittance has been maintained at an average of 10.99%.
Development Banks:
Development Bankers Association, an association of Development Bank Chief Executive Officers, also lowered the interest rate. The members of the committee have resolved to lower the deposit interest rate by 1%.
Now the interest rate on personal term deposits is 10.60 percent and the institutional term deposit interest rates have been lowered to 8.60 percent for a period over one year.
The average interest rate for remittance has been maintained at 11.60 percent.
Additionally, the savings interest rate has been reduced by 0.60 percentage points so the interest rates on savings of development banks will be 6 percent to 9 percent.
Finance Companies:
For the finance companies, the rates effective from Baishakh shall be 10.60 percent – 10.75 percent for individual fixed deposits. The average rates of the same for institutions is 8.75%.
On the other hand, the average interest rates for remittance has been maintained at 11.60-11.75 percent.
The interest rates on savings for finance companies has been maintained at an average rate of 8-9%.

Headline: ICRA Nepal places Issuer Rating of Garima Bikas Bank on watch with negative implications; revised rating ICRANP-IR BBB- indicates moderate credit risk
Full Content:
ICRA Nepal Limited has placed the Issuer Rating of Garima Bikas Bank Limited on watch with negative implications; revised rating is [ICRANP-IR] BBB-@ (pronounced as ICRA NP Issuer Rating Triple B minus). Issuers with this rating are considered to have a moderate degree of safety regarding timely servicing of financial obligations. Such issuers carry moderate credit risk. ‘@’ denotes rating on “watch with negative implication”
The Rating is only an opinion on the general creditworthiness of the rated entity and not specific to any particular debt instrument.
For the Rating categories [ICRANP-IR] AA through to [ICRANP-IR] C the sign of + (plus) or – (minus) may be appended to the Rating symbols to indicate their relative position within the Rating categories concerned. Thus, the Rating of [ICRANP-IR] BBB+ is one notch higher than [ICRANP-IR] BBB, while [ICRANP-IR] BBB- is one notch lower than [ICRANP-IR] BBB.

Headline: 75 Listed Companies from Different Sectors Have Already Declared Dividends for Fiscal Year 2078/2079; Know Them all?
Full Content:
Many companies listed in NEPSE have declared the dividend (both cash and bonus) for the fiscal year 2078/79. Proposed Dividend is the dividends that are distributed among the shareholders of the company during a financial year and will be paid in the Next Year. Hence, the dividends of last FY-78/79 are distributed in this FY-79/80.
Investors do not just earn from the rise in the share price of their portfolio stocks. They also earn from the dividend and bonuses announced by the company from time to time. Hence, it becomes important for secondary market enthusiasts to know the names of stocks that are going to pay dividends in near future.
Note for Beginners:
You can buy the shares of a company after it has proposed its dividend and still be eligible to get the dividend. In other words, you do not have to invest in the company for one whole fiscal year, which is a misconception among amateur investors.
The book closure date is simply the date on which the company closes its books for the dividend. Investors can still buy the shares after that date but they won’t get the dividend. To get the dividend of the company, you must buy the shares before the book closure date and you must not sell those shares till the book closure date. For example, investors can buy the shares of a company on the last day before its book closure date and still be entitled to the dividend. The investor remains eligible even if they sell the shares at the book closure date.
Commercial Banks
As of 7th December, 2022, 15 commercial banks have already proposed the dividend for the fiscal year 2078/79. Among them, Bank of Kathmandu has proposed the highest dividend, i.e. 20.95%. Similarly, Century Commercial Bank have paid the least dividend, i.e. 5%.
However, the book closure date for dividends most of these companies have already elapsed, meaning investors won't be able to claim the dividend of these companies. Whereas, Mega Bank's book closure date is on 9th December, 2022.
On the other hand, Book closure dates for SBL, SBI, NMB, PRVU and, CCBL is yet to be announced.
Cash and bonus dividends of companies proposed by the companies listed at NEPSE in the Fiscal Year 2078-79 are as given below.
Development Banks
Similarly, 4 of the total 16 development banks listed in NEPSE have declared the dividend for the fiscal year 2078/79. The book closure dates for all of them has not announced yet. As of now, Garima Bikas Bank  has declared the highest dividend viz. 14.5%.
Finance
Out of the listed finance corporations in Nepal, Only ICFC Finance Limited has declared dividends of the F.Y-78/79. Also, the book closure date of ICFC is yet to be announced.
Manufacturing and products
Out of the five companies in manufacturing & products sector, Unilever Nepal Limited declared a massive dividend of 1215%, which is wholly cash based. Also, the book closure dates of UNL and NLO has already elapsed.
Investments
Meanwhile, out of 5 listed only 2 investment companies have declared their dividend of FY-78/79.
Hotel and Tourism
From the hotel and tourism sector, only Soaltee Hotel Limited has declared dividend of 26.3158% of FY 78/79.
Mutual Funds
15 mutual funds have also unveiled the dividend. Sanima Equity Fund proposed the highest dividend of 22% for the fiscal year. However, the book closure date of all of these funds has elapsed.
Micro-Finance
5 out of 59 microfinance companies listed in NEPSE have declared the dividend for the fiscal year 2078/79. Jalpa Samudayik paid the highest dividend of 76.84% followed by Sana Kisan Laghubitta and RMDC paying 27.3684% of the dividend each (Both bonuses as well as cash for tax purpose).
However, the book closure dates for all these microfinance is not yet announced.
Hydropower
Out of the 60 listed hydropower companies, 9 hydropower companies have declared the dividend. As of now, Ridi Power Limited has paid the highest, i.e. 42.1%.
Non-Life Insurance
7 non life insurance companies have announced dividends of Fiscal Year 2078/79. United Insurance  has the highest dividend payout scale of 21.05%, whereas the lowest remains for Everest Insurance company. Both of these sectors have recently announced the date as their book closure date. Meanwhile, 2 out of the listed insurance company are yet to disclose their book closure date.
Merchant Bank
11 merchant banks have declared their dividends comprising of both cash as well as bonus dividends. NIC Asia remains at the top position while distributing its dividends. Whereas, Kumari Capital limited declared the least dividend of 5% only. Also, the book closure dates of these merchant banks are yet to be announced.
Disclaimer:
This article is intended to keep investors updated about the dividends declared by companies till now. It can be used to compare the trend of dividend proposals among companies and sectors. However, it should be noted that the dividend amount isn't the only valuation metric, and depending on it solely may result in speculation errors. Hence, higher dividend-paying stocks may already have a higher market price (hence reducing the profitability of buying).
Additionally, it is not owning more of something that has little value. Investors in NEPSE are overly attracted to bonus shares distribution, almost as if that is all that matters. As the legendary investor Mark Cuban puts it, a small stake in watermelon is more than 100% of a grape.

Headline: Net Profit of Development Banks of Nepal has Decreased in Q1; Dive Into Comprehensive Analysis of Major Indicators For All 15 Development Banks In Nepal
Full Content:
Without a doubt, the Financial Institutions are also experiencing economic instability as a result of market swings, given the increasing interest rates, inflation, and overall worldwide recession. Financial institutions' primary business revenue may be affected as a result of the monetary policy's higher interest rate bar, which may be advantageous for some financial institutions and detrimental for others. In this comprehensive analysis, we will examine the  financial performance of “B” class financial institution; Development Banks of Nepal, and see which institution is maintaining a good financial position despite numerous obstacles.
There are 16 development banks which are currently listed NEPSE. However, the Quarter first report (Q1) of
Saptakoshi Development Bank Limited (SAPDBL)
is not yet published by the company. Hence, this analysis discards SAPDBL.
So, let’s dissect the performance of B-class financial institutions based on the unaudited 1st quarterly report of 2079/80 fiscal year.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report,
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has reported the highest net profit for the period amounting to Rs. 30.70 Crores.
Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE)
comes in second place in terms of profit which amounts to Rs. 20.90 Crores.
The third position is secured by
Garima Bikas Bank Limited(GBBL)
with a net profit of Rs.
19.33
crores. In terms of growth in Net profit,
Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE)
has obtained growth margin of 42.18% for the Q1 of FY 79/80. However, 5 out of 8 National level development bank have reported decline in net profit as compared to the relevant quarter of previous year.
Coming towards regional level,
Miteri Development Bank Limited(MDB)
has reported highest net profit of Rs. 2.56 Crores, whereas
Corporate Development Bank Limited(CORBL)
has reported highest growth in net profit of 642.45% in the Q1 of F.Y 79/80.
Paid up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 5.66 Arba among all the development banks.
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL)
has the second-highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 4.58 Arba.
In the national level, SADBL has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 3.01 Arba and NABBC has only Rs. 26 Crores paid-up capital in the regional level.
Reserve and surplus:
Reserve is the amount that is retained by the company from its profits to promote future growth.
Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL)
has reported the highest reserve and surplus which amounts to Rs. 2.54 Arba. LBBL is followed by
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
with a reserve of Rs. 2.42 Arba.
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL)
has secured the third position with a reserve of 2.44 Arba.
Deposits from Customers:
In B-class institution,
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has topped the list with a total deposit of Rs. 1.05 Kharba. This list is followed by
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL)
with a total deposit of Rs. 68.97 Arba.
Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL)
has secured the third position with a total deposit of Rs. 53.92 Arba.
The overall development bank has collected a total deposit of Rs. 4.90 Kharba.
Loans and advances to Customers:
Till Q1 2079/2080, total loans and advances of development banks stood at Rs. 3.93 Kharba. The average loan stood at Rs. 27.98 Arba.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has disbursed the highest amount of loans which amounts to Rs. 88.03 Arba. Following the list,
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL)
has disbursed a total loan of Rs. 59.86 Arba.
Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL)
has disbursed a loan of Rs. 48.60 Arba which puts it in third place.
Net interest income:
Net Interest Income is the core business revenue which is calculated by subtracting the cost related to the deposits from the income from loans and advances.
In terms of Net interest income,
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
tops the list with a total of Rs.1.02 Arba.
Garima
Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL)
has the second-highest net interest income amounting to Rs. 79.62 Crores. GBBL is followed by
Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL)
which has reported a net interest income of Rs. 59.64 Crores.
Out of the 15 banks, 8 banks have reported above industry average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside a certain amount in loan loss provision and have delayed the loan repayment of several borrowers. A total of Rs 1.76 Arba has been shown in an impairment charge for a loan and other losses.
In the national level,
Garima
Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL)
has the highest impairment charge for a loan and other losses with Rs 28.13 Crores. Likewise,
Green Development Bank Limited(GRDBL)
in the regional level to have impairment charges of Rs.  3.84 Crores. Also,
Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE)
has reversal of impairment charges amounting to Rs. 4.98 Crores.
Earnings per share:
Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE)
topped the list in terms of EPS amounting to Rs. 22.12 per share.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has the second-highest EPS with Rs. 21.74 per share.
In the regional level,
Karnali
Development Bank Limited (KRBL)
reported highest EPS of Rs. 13.09 per share.
Out of 15 development banks, 7 banks have reported above industry average EPS.
Non-Performing Loan:
Non-performing loan indicates the risk of credit the bank provided to their clients. Higher NPL indicates that the bank might be at risk.
In terms of NPL,
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has the lowest ratio with an NPL of 0.77% and
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL)
has reported the highest NPL of 3.62% from the national level.
Likewise, in the regional level,
Sindhu
Bikas Bank Limited (SINDU) has reported the lowest NPL of 1.13%.
Out of 15 banks, 7 banks have reported below industry average NPL for this quarter. However, this is mainly because CORBL alone has massive NPL which led to increasing in average number.
One should calculate the industry average in terms of their own analysis model
.
P/E Ratio:
P/E ratio tells investors what they are paying for each Rupee of earnings of the firm. The lower the ratio, the better the deal.
In terms of the P/E ratio,
Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE)
has the lowest P/E ratio of 12.72 times. This means that you are paying Rs. 12.72 for every Rupee of earning of Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE).
Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL)
reported a P/E of 59.15 times from the national level and
Sindhu Bikas Bank Limited (SINDHU)
has reported P/E ratio of 169.72 times in the regional level.
One should always check the fundamentals of the company and if they found the bad fundamentals then there is a reason for the lower valuation. Also the PE is calculated as per the quarter end closing price of the respective companies. In today's date the price differs in the secondary market.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by
Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL)
with Rs. 174.02 per share. This is followed by
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL)
with a net worth per share of Rs. 161.02 per share. Likewise,
Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB)
reported a net worth of Rs. 146.07 per share making it the highest in the regional level.
The average net worth per share comes at Rs. 134.50 per share when we factor in all the net worth per share of all the 15 banks.

Headline: Existing Promoter Shareholders Of Garima Bikas Bank Auctioning 1,09,811 Unit Promoter Shares From Today
Full Content:
The existing promoters of
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL)
are auctioning 1,09,811 unit promoter shares to the shareholders from today i.e 26th Shrawan and will conclude on 31st Bhadra, 2079.

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank Distributed 16% Bonus Shares to Demat Accounts

The 270th meeting of the board of directors held on Poush 22, 2078 decided to distribute the entirety of the dividend in bonus shares. The paid-up capital of the company during dividend distribution was Rs. 3.94 arba Thus, the bonus shares were worth slightly over Rs. 63.17 crores. According to the notice, shareholders who bought the shares after the commencement of joint operation (28th Kartik, 2078) will have to pay the tax amount on the dividend proposed and only after submitting the tax amount to be paid, the bonus shares will be distributed to the particular DEMAT account .

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank's Q4 Highlights: Net Profit Crosses Rs 1 Arba; NPL Below 1 and EPS at Rs 23.07

The bank's Net Interest Income (core business income) has increased by 31.67% to Rs. 2.61 Arba compared to the corresponding quarter of the previous year.
The bank’s paid-up capital stands at Rs. 4.57 Arba with Rs. 2.04 Arba in Reserve and surplus. The Non-performing loan (NPL) slightly increased to 0.85% from 0.72% in the corresponding quarter.
The earnings per share (EPS) of the Bank stood at Rs. 23.07 and Net worth per share stood at Rs. 144.57. The company traded at a P/E multiple of 16.77 times.
The Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) of the bank stands at 13.49%.

Headline: The Interest Rates Of Banks and Financial Institutions For The Month Of Ashad Remains Unchanged
Full Content:
Commercial banks
have kept their interest rate profile unchanged in Ashad. The maximum interest rate on fixed deposits provided by commercial banks is 11.03%. The tenure for such fixed deposits is above three months or above six months, depending upon the banks.
Most banks had interest rates of 11.03% for tenure above three months. However, for Standard Chartered and Nepal SBI Bank, the interest rates on fixed deposits were fixed according to the time frame. For standard chartered, the interest rate was 10.3% for periods of less than three months and 11.03% for periods higher than three months. Likewise, Nepal SBI had fixed its rates as; 6.6% above three months, 8.8% above six months, 11.03% above one year, and 9.95% above two years.
Most commercial banks provide a 6.03% interest rate p.a. for depositors on savings.
In contrast, institutions were offered a maximum of 10.03% on fixed deposits.
Since Chaitra, commercial banks had constant deposit interest rates. Individual deposits receive a maximum interest rate of 11.03 percent, while institutional deposits receive a maximum interest rate of 10.03 percent. Senders of remittances are given an interest rate of 12.03 percent.
Likewise, development banks
, have also not raised the interest rates on deposits. The highest interest rate for individuals on fixed deposits is 12% and this rate for institutional depositors remains at 11%.
Similarly, most of the development banks interest rates on savings accounts for the month of Ashad is 7%.
Finance Companies
interest rates on deposits also remain constant. The highest interest rate for individuals on fixed deposits is 12.25% and the rate for institutional depositors is  11.25%.
For savings accounts, each finance company has a varied range of interest rates. While the average rate of interest on savings accounts for most finance institutions for the month of Ashad is 8% p.a., few companies are also offering greater interest rates up to 9%.

Headline: Detailed Summary Of Dividends Distributed By Sectors Listed In Nepse For FY-77/78 With Exact Dividend Figures
Full Content:
Companies listed in NEPSE have declared the dividend (both cash and bonus) for the fiscal year 2078/79. Proposed Dividend is the dividends that are distributed among the shareholders of the company during a financial year and will be paid in the Next Year. Hence, the dividends of last FY-77/78 are distributed in this FY-78/79.
Investors do not just earn from the rise in the share price of their portfolio stocks. They also earn from the dividend and bonuses announced by the company from time to time. Hence, it becomes important for secondary market enthusiasts to know the names of stocks that are going to pay dividends in near future.
Note for Beginners:
You can buy the shares of a company after it has proposed its dividend and still be eligible to get the dividend. In other words, you do not have to invest in the company for one whole fiscal year, which is a misconception among amateur investors.
The book closure date is simply the date on which the company closes its books for the dividend. Investors can still buy the shares after that date but they won’t get the dividend. To get the dividend of the company, you must buy the shares before the book closure date and you must not sell those shares till the book closure date. For example, investors can buy the shares of a company on the last day before its book closure date and still be entitled to the dividend. The investor remains eligible even if they sell the shares at the book closure date.

Headline: Garima Bikas Bank Reports Satisfactory Growth In Profitability Indicators In Q3
Full Content:

The annualized earnings per share (EPS) of the Bank stood at Rs. 22.84 and Net worth per share stood at Rs. 128.08. The company traded at a P/E multiple of 17.95 times.
